Yu's proofs of these items work on the Galois side over F_q(X_1). findings.claim: For gcd(e, n) > 1, item 119 and the brief say Théorème 1.4 'must be imported from Mellit [Me17]'. Mellit's theorem does not state it. Mellit proves that the number A_{g,r,d} of absolutely indecomposable bundles of rank r and degree d does not depend on d. Yu's Théorème 1.4 is about the number P_n^e of isocline bundles. The passage from one to the other is a separate argument that neither Yu nor any item supplies. Let e/n = e'/n' in lowest terms. An isocline bundle is a multiset of indecomposable bundles over F_q of slope e'/n'. An indecomposable bundle E of rank rn' and degree re' has End(E) local with residue field F_{q^d}, where d | r, and E ⊗ F_{q^d} is the sum of the d Frobenius conjugates of an absolutely indecomposable bundle of rank rn'/d and degree re'/d. So P_n^e is a Möbius and plethystic expression in the numbers A_{g,rn'/d}(X_m). By Mellit's degree independence (item 046) it therefore depends only on n' = n/gcd(n, e), that is, on the order of e in Z/nZ. Item 119 does not even depend on item 046. Also: Item 119 says that for gcd(e,n) > 1 Théorème 1.4 'must be imported from Mellit [Me17]', and the route 12 brief says 'the general case of Théorème 1.4 is Mellit's theorem'. But Mellit's theorem is about A_{g,r,d}, the number of geometrically indecomposable bundles, while Théorème 1.4 is about P_n^e, the number of isocline bundles. The two differ when gcd(e,n) > 1: for n = 2, e = 0, every L_1 ⊕ L_2 with deg L_1 = deg L_2 = 0 is isocline and decomposable, so it is counted by P_2^0 and not by A_{g,2,0}. Importing Mellit therefore leaves a step that no item states: P_n^e is the T^n coefficient of a product over the ranks r with re/n ∈ Z of factors built from the counts of indecomposables over F_q, and by Krull–Schmidt and Galois descent these are combinations of A_{g, r/k, re/(nk)}(X_l). Writing e/n = e′/n′ in lowest terms, r = tn′, gcd(r, re/n) = t, so once A is independent of the degree the product depends only on n and n′ = n/gcd(e,n).

findings.claim: The paper obtains (5.3.8) in one line, 'En appliquant le corollaire 4.2.6 pour e = −1', but Corollaire 4.2.6 does not apply as stated, and two compensating signs are left unmentioned. (i) By (5.3.7) the cone function is 1̂^{−1}_Q(μ) = (−1)^{dim a_Q^G}(∏μ_i)θ_Q(μ)^{−1}, not θ_Q(μ)^{−1}; this contributes (−1)^m with m = dim a_L^G. (ii) The family in (5.3.8) is μ ↦ n_{Q|Q_L}(π, λλ_w/μ)/n_{Q|Q_L}(π, λλ_w), a function of λ/μ, while Corollaire 4.2.6 treats μ ↦ c_Q(λμ)/c_Q(λ). Writing c_α(z) = f_α(u_α/z)/f_α(u_α) with u_α = λ^{α^∨} and f_α(u) = ∏_{β|α} n_β(π, λ_w^{β^∨}u), one has c'_α(1) = −u_α f'_α(u_α)/f_α(u_α), so Théorème 4.2.4 gives lim Σ_Q θ_Q(μ)^{−1}c_Q(μ) = (−1)^m Σ_F ∏_{α∈F} u_α f'_α(u_α)/f_α(u_α), since |F| = m. The two factors (−1)^m cancel, and Lemme 4.2.5 with the argument principle then gives Σ_F ∏(N(n_α) − P(n_α)). So (5.3.8) and Proposition 5.1.1 are correct, but the step is a gap the extraction does not record, and no item supplies the variant of Corollaire 4.2.6 that the proof of item 067 actually uses. A formaliser applying item 054 literally gets the wrong sign whenever dim a_L^G is odd and only one of the two signs is noticed.

En appliquant le corollaire 4.2.6 pour e = −1, on obtient (5.3.8) ∫_{Im X^G_L} lim_{µ→1} Σ_{Q∈P(L)} 1̂^e_Q(µ) n_{Q|Q_L}(π, λλ_w/µ)/n_{Q|Q_L}(π, λλ_w) dλ = Σ_F ∏_{α∈F}(N(n_α(π,·)) − P(n_α(π,·))) ... car |λ_w^{β∨}| = 1'. p. 40: 'c_α(z) = ∏_{β|α} n_β(π,(λλ_w)^{β∨}/z)/n_β(π,(λλ_w)^{β∨}) si α ∈ −Φ_{Q_L}'. p. 27, Corollaire 4.2.6: '∫_{Im X^G_M} lim_{µ→1} Σ_Q θ_Q(µ)^{−1} c_Q(λµ)/c_Q(λ) dλ = Σ_F ∏_{β∈F}(N(c_β) − P(c_β))'. findings.claim: Item 122 adds the hypothesis that P takes integer values 'for all choices of paired eigenvalues', and its note says the re-indexing in the proof makes this necessary ('the hypothesis is needed for all choices (or P must be W-invariant)'). It is not needed: the curve the proof uses has zeta numerator with Galois group S_g ⋉ (S_2)^g (condition (2′)), which acts on its 2g Weil numbers through every pair-preserving permutation. An integer value is Galois-invariant, so if P(p^{mk}, σ_1^k, …, σ_g^k) ∈ Z for one indexing with σ_iσ_{i+g} = q, the value is the same for every such indexing, and the re-indexing of p. 81 is justified.
